title: Algebraic and analytic structure of Morikawa's sangaku problem
summary: Let $μ(r)$ denote the minimal side length of a square inscribed in the curvilinear triangular region formed by two tangent circles of radii $1$ and $r \ge 1$ together with their common tangent line. The problem of finding a closed-form expression for $μ(r)$ was posed in early nineteenth-century Japan by Morikawa. It was proved by Holly and Krumm (2021) that no expression in radicals exists for $μ(r)$.
